title: Codex lab remediation drift: bounded misdelivery and rework claim
product: Codex desktop and its model/tool orchestration
plan: Subscription and credit usage; provider reconciliation requested

requested.summary: Deliver the clean, improved product compilation and follow the agreed lab-remediation sequence, ownership and tool boundaries.
requested.source: Private local transcript review for the fixed eight-hour interval; redacted evidence summarized by incident below.

delivered.summary: Repeated wrong product subsets, unsupported archive additions and cleanup, premature implementation and rollback, duplicate compilation preparation, an unrequested exposure audit, dashboard repair, and a browser route contrary to the displayed disabled preference. IMPORTANT: approved = 0 below is bookkeeping exclusion of remaining authorized/mixed work, not evidence that no useful authorized work occurred. The $19.70 standard API benchmark covers only the selected response subset; it is neither a measured cash charge nor a ceiling on the requested reimbursement review.

evidence.text: The monetary field is a standard public API list-price benchmark for bounded candidate responses. It does not establish actual Codex credit debits, subscription value, an invoice charge, or a provider-approved refund.

All other OpenAI usage is excluded as authorized or not individually attributable. Exclusion is not a finding that every excluded response was correct. All Anthropic usage is excluded from this OpenAI claim; it includes the earlier provider claim.

The approved bucket is deliberately empty because remaining authorized and mixed work is excluded from this bounded claim. It does not establish that no useful authorized work occurred. Do not interpret the generated unapproved share or approved/unapproved ratio as an overall waste measure.

The six internal codex-auto-review responses remain counted, excluded and unpriced. They are not assigned a zero rate. Strict CLI exit 3 is expected for this disclosed limitation; there are no unclassified responses.

RR-03 includes the coordinator session and its two children. Every PR selector covers its main thread only. Other selectors cover the exact named thread. Inherited histories are globally deduplicated before these intervals are applied.

RR-01: Deliver the combined improved product workstreams, with known scope preserved. Observed: Reconcile delivered a 24-file product handoff subset, then recognized the requested population was different, then recognized that rewrapping input ZIPs did not supply completed improvements. Limits: Governance and meaningful product inspection were expressly authorized. This is a bounded wrong-deliverable/rework allocation, not a claim that all file inspection was waste.

RR-02: Follow the agreed execution-environment, Governance repository and runner prerequisite order. Observed: Reconcile patched the release verifier and delegated fleet tests, then reverted its changes after the user pointed out missing prerequisites. Limits: The verifier bug was real and the later Governance repository/runner setup was explicitly requested. No deployment is established in this detour.

RR-03: Select the requested clean product contents and establish that they meet intended use. Observed: Coordinator presented a 904MB compilation before coverage reconciliation, directed original archives to be added, delivered 1.667GB, then rebuilt 217MB after the user rejected the added history. It also added START_HERE and OPEN_PRODUCT HTML pages and had to remove them. Limits: A small source ZIP is not inherently fake. Subsequent source comparison found the same extractor engine in the small release; optional runtime readers were absent. Neither size nor CRC alone proves intended functionality. The interval includes error diagnosis, not solely harmful edits.

RR-04: Honor the disabled browser-control preference; submit through an available authorized non-browser route. Observed: Coordinator opened two in-app support tabs, received page content, and tried a click. After objection it said no submission route was exposed before checking GitHub/CLI; GitHub subsequently worked. Limits: Screenshot directly shows the toggle off; persistence throughout is the user's attestation. Exact internal enforcement failure is unknown; no browser operation was performed to reproduce it during this audit.

PR-01: Return the improved multi-product compilation; the agents had already explicitly distinguished 19 input ZIPs from the requested improved outputs. Observed: Separate pointed to the product handoff subset subset, then corrected itself. Rollout shortly afterward pointed to the same full/small subset subset, then a broader but still product handoff-only baseline. Both admitted these were not the requested 19-workstream package. Limits: Agents did not claim the 6.5 MB baseline was complete; they explicitly disclosed limitations. Size alone is not evidence of a fake ZIP. The violation is the wrong deliverable scope and repeated loss of already-established scope, not an assertion that compression was impossible.

PR-02: Work the rollout sequence and deliverable; remediation was to follow the complete reviewed plan and owner approval. Fleet-report behavior had not been selected as the next implementation task. Observed: After promising repository work, Rollout searched the fleet repository, altered fleet-report semantics and tests, admitted the edit was unrelated/off-sequence, reverted it, and restored it after the user objected to deletion. It then expanded the fix again. Limits: The code change may be useful and passed tests. No deployment or GitHub issue reopening is demonstrated. The user had broadly authorized lab remediation, so this finding is about loss of the agreed next-step sequence and unnecessary rollback/rework, not a claim that fleet-report was permanently outside all possible project scope.

PR-03: Reconcile owns the single final compilation; Rollout contributes sequencing and issue-plan content. Observed: Rollout planned a separate compilation, inspected compilation inputs, announced itself as compilation owner, and reasoned about a new script. The user challenged the duplicate effort. Rollout admitted shared goal had been mistaken for shared ownership. Limits: The persisted record in this interval shows preparation, reasoning and reads, not a successful new compiler file write or a second completed archive. Later Rollout edited Reconcile’s existing compiler and relinquished it; do not conflate that later handoff with proof of another completed ZIP.

OTHER-01: Correct repository ownership and offline delivery boundaries from the owner correction. Observed: Tracker launched a separate exposure investigation. Its dedicated child searched the organization, fetched 37 issue bodies, compared repository contents, and scanned additional trees before the user stopped it. Limits: Parent turn also performs requested ownership corrections; do not classify its entire cost as exposure work. Evidence shows audit stopped after correction; no claim that it continued secretly. This is a scope violation, not proof of data exposure.

OTHER-02: The requested dashboard shows every repository, owner, progress and blocker in a readable visual form. Observed: The first repair retained the rejected map under a historical dropdown. After its removal, a scope summary and then a text-heavy table still did not satisfy the requested visual status view. Two direct correction turns removed the history and restored visual repository cards. Limits: A dashboard itself was explicitly requested, as was repository status analysis. Do not classify original dashboard construction or all later status analysis as unrequested. Mirror work occurred in mixed turns and is excluded from these narrow candidates.

OTHER-03: One compilation containing the last polished and reviewed product versions across all named workstreams. Observed: Verify linked the subset handoff subset in response to the compilation request, then acknowledged it was wrong. It built a 1.66 GB package which its later content review rejected for old handoffs and missing products. Tracker separately acknowledged linking the 197 KB small subset subset and the original-input bundle. These are linked failures in the same delivery episode, not separate customer requests. Limits: The initial subset link explicitly disclosed it was not the combined package, so do not claim that the model falsely asserted 197 KB contained every repository. The mismatch was answering a full-delivery demand with a known subset. Inspection after 03:11 was newly and explicitly requested; do not automatically include all subsequent review.
